Programme: MASTER OF COMPUTER APPLICATIONS

Subject: Probability and Statistics

Max. Marks: 100
FINAL EXAMINATION (Acad. Year:2025-2026)
Instructions:
1. This question paper contains 9 pages.
2. Answer to each new question to be started on a fresh page.
3. Figure in right hand side indicates full marks
4. Questions 1 is compulsory.
5. Solve any four out of remaining six questions
6. In all, 5 questions to be attempted
7. All questions carry equal marks.
8. Assume Suitable data if necessary.
9. Use of scientific calculator is allowed.
Answer the following:   Marks
CO1;BL1   Q.1 a. A discrete random variable has the following probability distribution:
X   -3   -2   -1   0   1   2
P(X = x)   k   2k   0.2   3k   0.1   2k   [4]
Find k and P( -2 < X < 1).
CO1;BL2   b.   The joint probability distribution of X and Y is given by:
[4]
P(X= x, Y= y) = k(3x + 2y), where x = 0,1,2 and y = 1,2,3
Estimate k and marginal probability distributions of X.
CO1;BL1   c.   Identify the type of correlation in each of the following cases:
(i)   𝑏𝑦𝑥= 1 , 𝑏𝑥𝑦= 2   [4]
2
(ii)   r² - 1 = 0
(iii)   r = -0.5
CO1;BL1   d.   A bag contains 5 yellow balls, 4 black balls, and 3 white balls. One ball
is drawn at random from the bag. Find the probability that the ball drawn
is:   [4]
(i) black
(ii) not white
CO1;BL1   e.   A random sample of 50 items gives a mean of 4.8 and standard deviation
6.0. Test whether the sample is drawn from a normal population with   [4]
mean 5 at 5% level of significance.
CO1;BL2   Q.2 a. The recovery rate of patients suffering from a certain disease is believed
to be 82%. In a particular hospital, out of 500 patients treated during a
year, 435 recovered. Can the hospital be considered efficient at 5% level   [6]
of significance?
CO2;BL1   b.   The joint probability density function is given by:   [6]
f(x,y) = kx²y, 0 ≤ x ≤ 1, 0 ≤ y ≤ 2
********** 1 **********
--- page 2 ---
Estimate:
(i) the value of k (ii) P(X ≤ 1/2, Y ≤ 1)
CO3;BL3   c.   A random variable with probability density function is given below
𝑓(𝑥) =    𝑘 𝑥2        0 < 𝑥< 1   [8]
=     0             elsewhere
Calculate k, mean and variance.
CO3;BL3   Q.3 a. A die is thrown twice.
A: The number obtained on the first throw is even
B: The sum of the two numbers is greater than 8
Find:
(i) P(A)   [6]
(ii) P(B)
(iii) P(A ∩ B)
(iv) P(B|A)
(v) Check whether A and B are independent.
CO2;BL2   b.   The means of two simple samples of 1000 and 2000 items are 170 cm
and 169 cm respectively. Can the samples be regarded as drawn from
the same population with standard deviation 10 cm at 5% level of   [6]
significance?
CO3;BL3   c.   Suppose X is a discrete random variable and has a probability mass
function as follows:
X   0   1   2
P(X= x)   1/3   1/3   1/3   [8]
Determine the moment generating function and hence find mean,
variance.
CO2;BL1   Q.4 a. A machine produces items with a probability of defect equal to 0.1. If 8
items are selected at random, estimate:
[6]
(i) Probability that exactly 2 items are defective
(ii) Probability that at most 2 items are defective
CO4;BL5   b.   A machinist is expected to make engine parts with axle diameter of 1.75
cm. A random sample of 10 parts shows a mean diameter 1.85 cm with
an SD of 0.1 cm. On the basis of this sample, Test whether the work of   [6]
the machinist is inferior.
CO4;BL3   c.   The following are the marks obtained by 10 students in Mathematics and
Statistics. Using the least squares method, find the regression line of Y
on X.   [8]
X 52 55 57 54 58 56 60 59 61 53
Y 48 50 52 49 53 51 55 54 56 47
********** 2 **********
--- page 3 ---
CO2;BL5   Q.5 a. A sample of size 12 gave a variance as 4.2 while another sample of size
16 gave a variance as 2.8. Check whether the two samples be regarded as   [6]
drawn from populations having the same variance at 5% LOS.
CO1;BL2   b.   The sugar contents in two random samples of a beverage are given
below:
Sample 1 18 20 21 22 24   [6]
Sample 2 19 23 25 26 27 30
Test whether the two samples have the same mean.
CO2;BL2   c.   The diameters of steel rods produced in a factory are normally
distributed with mean 50 mm and standard deviation 2 mm.
Compute:
[8]
(i) The probability that a rod has diameter between 48 mm and 53 mm
(ii) The probability that a rod has diameter greater than 54 mm
(iii) The percentage of rods having diameter less than expectation.
CO3;BL3   Q.6 a. The probability that a machine works properly is 0.85, given that it was
serviced. The probability that it works properly without servicing is 0.30.
Assume that the probability that the machine was serviced is 0.70. Apply   [6]
Bayes’ theorem to find the probability that the machine was serviced
given that it works properly.
CO4;BL2   b.   Evaluate Karl Pearson’s correlation coefficient from the following
values using deviation method:
X 14 18 22 26 30 34 38   [6]
Y 8   11 14 17 20 23 26
CO4;BL5   c.   A company has three training programs, and the management wants to
determine whether there is a difference in the average performance
scores of employees under the three programs. The following data are
the scores of five randomly selected employees from each program.
Analyze whether there is any significant difference in the means using
one-way ANOVA test at 5% significant level.
Program (Performance Scores)
Program 1 Program 2 Program 3
[8]
42   50   40
45   52   41
44   49   39
43   51   42
46   53   38

x   0   1   2   3   4
f   20   32   26   14   8

Treatment   Infected   Not Infected
Vaccine   95   25
No Vaccine   70   30   [8]
Discuss the association of vaccination and infection using chi-square test
at 5% LOS.

Answer the following:   Marks
CO1;BL1   Q.1 a. A discrete random variable X has the following probability distribution:
X   0   1   2   3   [4]
P(X=x) A   2A   3A   B
If the mean of X is 1.5, identify the values of A and B.
CO1;BL2   b.   The joint probability distribution of X and Y is given by:
P(X=x, Y=y) = k(3x + 4y), where x = 1,2,3 and y = 0,1,2.
Find:   [4]
(i) the value of k (ii) the marginal probability distribution of X.
CO1;BL1   c.   Identify the type of correlation in each of the following cases:
(i) r = +1   [4]
(ii) r = -0.62
(iii) 2r² + r - 3 = 0
CO1;BL1   d.   If three coins are thrown, find the probability of getting:
(i) exactly two heads   [4]
(ii) at least two heads
CO1;BL1   e.   A random sample of 100 items is taken from a population with known
standard deviation σ = 10. The sample mean is found to be 52. State
whether the population mean is greater than 50 at 5% level of   [4]
significance.
CO1;BL2   Q.2 a.   In a survey, 200 out of 500 men were found to prefer a product, while
180 out of 400 women preferred the same product. Find whether the   [6]
proportions of men and women who prefer the product are equal at 5%
level of significance.
CO2;BL1   b.   The joint probability density function is:
f(x,y) = kxy, 0 ≤ x ≤ 2, 0 ≤ y ≤ 1   [6]
Estimate: (i) k
(ii) P(X ≤ 1, Y ≤ 1/2)
********** 1 **********
--- page 2 ---
CO3;BL3   c.
A continuous random variable X has the probability density function:
f(x) = kx(2 - x), 0 ≤ x ≤ 2   [8]
= 0,   otherwise.
Calculate k, mean & variance.
CO3;BL3   Q.3 a. Two fair dice are thrown simultaneously.
Let A be the event that the sum of the numbers is even.
Let B be the event that at least one die shows 4.   [6]
Determine P(A), P(A ∩ B) & Find P(A|B).
CO2;BL2   b.   A sample of 100 students from college A has mean score 68 with sample
standard deviation 10. A sample of 120 students from college B has
mean score 65 with sample standard deviation 12. Test at 5% level of   [6]
significance whether there is a significant difference between the mean
scores of the two colleges.
CO3;BL3   c.   A discrete random variable X with probability distribution:
X   0   1   2
P(X=x) 1/4   1/2   1/4   [8]
Determine Moment Generating Function (MGF), Coefficient of
Skewness & Kurtosis
CO2;BL1   Q.4 a.   In a communication network, the number of packet errors per minute
follows a Poisson distribution with mean 2.
Estimate:   [6]

CO-1;   a. A bag contains 6 white, 5 black, and 3 red balls. Three balls are drawn one [3]

BL -2   (i) all the balls drawn are black,

CO-   b. A discrete random variable 𝑋 has the following probability mass function:   [4]
2,3,4;   𝑋   0   1   2   3   4   5   6   7
SO-1;
𝑃(𝑋)   0   𝑘   2𝑘   2𝑘   3𝑘   𝑘2   2𝑘2   7𝑘2 + 𝑘
BL-2
Determine

Q.1)
CO-1;   a) A container has 8 apples, 5 oranges, and 7 bananas. One fruit is selected. Find the [4]
SO-1;   probability that the (i) fruit is not a banana, (ii) fruit is either apple or banana.
BL-2
CO-2,3,4; b) During an audit of a printed-circuit-board assembly line, the inspector assigns a [4]
SO-1;   defect-severity score X to each board. The probability mass function is:
BL-2   X   0   1   2   3   4   5   6
P(X=x)   k   3k   5k   7k   9k   11k   13k
Determine the value of k, distribution function, P(X < 4), and P(3 < X ≤ 6).
CO-2,4;   c) The first four raw moments of a random variable X about the origin are 1, 5, 25, [4]
SO-1;   and 140 respectively. Evaluate first four central moments of X.
BL-4
CO-2,3,5; d) A random sample of 180 batteries showed an average life of 920 hours with a [4]
SO-1;   standard deviation of 140 hours. Test at 5% level of significance whether the
BL-3   batteries belong to a population with mean life 950 hours.
CO-2,4;   e) The regression lines of a sample are 𝑥+ 2𝑦−6 = 0 and 3𝑥+ 𝑦−7 = 0. Find [4]
SO-1;   mean of x, mean of y, regression coefficient of x on y and regression coefficient
BL-3   of y on x.
Q.2)
CO-2,4;   a) A retail company wants to examine whether weather conditions influence [6]
SO-1;   consumer demand for seasonal products. During the summer season, the
BL-3   management recorded the daily maximum temperature (in °C) and the
corresponding number of ice cream packs sold at one of its stores over 8 selected
days. The collected data are given below:
Daily Temperature (X) (°C) 24   26   28   30   29   27   31   32
Ice Cream Sales (Y) (packs) 120 135 150 165 160 145 170 180
Calculate Karl Pearson’s coefficient of correlation between daily temperature and
ice cream sales.

--- page 2 ---
CO-2,3,4; b) During a quality control study in a manufacturing unit, the number of defects X [6]
SO-1;   observed in randomly selected items was recorded. The following frequency
BL-2   distribution was obtained based on a sample of items inspected:
X   0   1   2   3   4
f   5   29   36   25   5
Fit a binomial distribution to the data and calculate the theoretical frequencies.
CO-2,3,5; c) A study compared the average daily internet usage of students in two universities. [8]
SO-1;   A sample of 200 students from University A showed a mean usage of 4.8 hours per
BL-3   day with a standard deviation of 1.5 hours. A sample of 180 students from
University B showed a mean usage of 4.3 hours per day with a standard deviation
of 1.6 hours. Test at 5% level of significance whether the mean daily internet usage
of students in the two universities differs significantly.
Q.3)
CO-2,3,4; a) A manufacturing company produces electrical resistors that are used in precision [6]
SO-1;   electronic circuits. To ensure consistency and reliability, the company conducts
BL-2   quality testing on a batch of 300 resistors. It is observed that the resistance values
(in ohms) of these resistors follow a normal distribution with mean 200 ohms and
standard deviation 20 ohms. Estimate the percentage of resistors having resistance
(i) greater than 240 ohms, (ii) less than 170 ohms, (iii) between 180 ohms and 220
ohms.
CO-2,4;   b) Calculate the rank coefficient of correlation from the following data:   [6]
SO-1;   X   8   10   10   12   14   16   18
BL-3   Y   55   60   63   70   72   80   82
CO-2,3,5; c) A survey was conducted to study the relationship between educational [8]
SO-1;   qualification and type of employment (Private, Government, Self-employed). The
BL-4   data collected is as follows:
Qualification   Private   Government   Self-employed   Total
Graduate   80   50   120   250
Non-Graduate   60   40   50   150
Total   140   90   170   400
Use the Chi-square test at 5% level of significance to test whether qualification
and type of employment are independent.
Q.4)
CO-2,4;   a) A multi-specialty hospital wishes to examine how the waiting time of patients [6]
SO-1;   before consultation affects their overall satisfaction with the service provided. A
BL-2   survey was conducted among 6 patients and following data were obtained:

Satisfaction Score (Y) (out of 100)   90   82   75   68   60   52
Determine the regression line of satisfaction score on waiting time and estimate
the satisfaction score of a patient whose waiting time is 22 minutes.

1   0.1   0.1   0.05   0.05
2   0.05   0.2   0.05   0.1

(iii) P(X < 2, Y ≤3).

Q.5)

BL-2   determine the probability it was produced by machine C.

CO-2,3,5; c) A hospital studies the effectiveness of three different treatments (A, B, and C) by [8]
SO-1;   recording the recovery time (in days) of patients:
BL-4   Treatment A:   10   12   11   9   10

At the 5% level of significance, test whether the mean recovery time differs

Q.6)
CO-2,3,4; a) A factory manufacturing LED bulbs finds that 0.15% of bulbs are defective during [6]
SO-1;   production. The bulbs are packed in boxes containing 600 bulbs each. A wholesaler

defective bulbs.
CO-1;   b) In a company, 60% of employees uses email regularly, 50% uses messaging apps, [6]
SO-1;   and 35% uses both. (i) Find the probability that a messaging app user also uses

Q.1)
CO-1;   a) A container has 8 apples, 5 oranges, and 7 bananas. One fruit is selected. Find the [4]
SO-1;   probability that the (i) fruit is not a banana, (ii) fruit is either apple or banana.
BL-2
CO-2,3,4; b) During an audit of a printed-circuit-board assembly line, the inspector assigns a [4]
SO-1;   defect-severity score X to each board. The probability mass function is:
BL-2   X   0   1   2   3   4   5   6
P(X=x)   k   3k   5k   7k   9k   11k   13k
Determine the value of k, distribution function, P(X < 4), and P(3 < X ≤ 6).
CO-2,4;   c) The first four raw moments of a random variable X about the origin are 1, 5, 25, [4]
SO-1;   and 140 respectively. Evaluate first four central moments of X.
BL-4
CO-2,3,5; d) A random sample of 180 batteries showed an average life of 920 hours with a [4]
SO-1;   standard deviation of 140 hours. Test at 5% level of significance whether the
BL-3   batteries belong to a population with mean life 950 hours.
CO-2,4;   e) The regression lines of a sample are 𝑥+ 2𝑦−6 = 0 and 3𝑥+ 𝑦−7 = 0. Find [4]
SO-1;   mean of x, mean of y, regression coefficient of x on y and regression coefficient
BL-3   of y on x.
Q.2)
CO-2,4;   a) A retail company wants to examine whether weather conditions influence [6]
SO-1;   consumer demand for seasonal products. During the summer season, the
BL-3   management recorded the daily maximum temperature (in °C) and the

mathematical abilities than the average student in the district? (table value:1.645) (10 Marks)
